name: Sawtooth Range Scramble

pitch_detail.notes: Loose, exposed traverse under the west face of The Fin
pitch_detail.pitch: Approach scramble (below Sawtooth Pass to Horn's notch)

pitch_detail.notes: ~130 ft; standard alpine rack; An impressive powering mass of stone - don't let the modest grade cause overconfidence

descent_text: Descend by rappelling from the summit notch — carrying two ropes allows a full double-rope rappel back down to the notch south of The Horn — then reverse the scramble under The Fin's west face to regain the ridge. Parties completing the fuller Sawtooth Ridge traverse have described the eventual descent off the ridge system as a brushy, slow 'controlled fall' through slide alder and devil's club; expect the broader cross-country return to Flapjack Lakes/Gladys Divide to be vegetated and time-consuming regardless of exact line.
approach: Drive Hwy 101 to Hoodsport, then SR-119 (North Lake Cushman Road, becomes FR-24 past the lake) roughly 9 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station/trailhead (~800 ft) in the SE corner of Olympic National Park. Hike the North Fork Skokomish River Trail ~3.4 miles to the Spike Camp junction, then climb steeply another ~3.6 miles to Flapjack Lakes (~4,000 ft, 8 miles from the trailhead) — a limited-entry wilderness camping zone, so reserve a permit well ahead. From Flapjack Lakes, follow the Gladys Divide trail to about 4,400 ft, then leave it and climb cross-country southeast toward Sawtooth Pass to reach the base of The Fin and The Horn. Round-trip approach mileage to Gladys Divide alone runs close to 19 miles with roughly 4,000+ ft of net gain, before the additional ridge travel and the climb itself — this is realistically a backpack-in with a high camp, not a day trip from the road.
overview: The Horn is a rugged basalt pinnacle on Sawtooth Ridge, in the far southeastern corner of Olympic National Park on the crest between Mount Cruiser and Mount Lincoln — east of Flapjack Lakes, not in the Lake of the Angels/Putvin drainage to the north (a different part of the southeastern Olympics). It shares its approach (Staircase, Flapjack Lakes, Gladys Divide) with Mount Cruiser and The Fin. Though it has been called a Class 3-4 scramble, parties agree it is a genuine roped 5th-class trad route (5.5, R) on some of the best pillow basalt the Olympic Range has to offer, with real exposure and sparse protection.
beta: Above Flapjack Lakes, the standard approach leaves the Gladys Divide trail at about 4,400 ft, short of the divide near a small pond, and climbs an open snow/rock slope southeast toward Sawtooth Pass - snow lingers on it into midsummer, so carry an axe early in the season. Below the pass, traverse right on loose, exposed class 3-4 ground under the west face of The Fin to the notch south of The Horn. Do not underestimate The Horn as a simple scramble: despite the modest 5.5 grade, the final summit pitch is run-out and the rock demands careful gear placement.
gear: Rack to 3 inches (doubles in common finger/hand sizes useful)
A few small pitons and tat/cord for aging fixed anchors
Two ropes, for a double-rope rappel off the summit notch
Helmet — loose rock increases in frequency near Sawtooth Pass
Full overnight backpacking kit — the approach is a multi-day undertaking, not a day trip
fa: Ruth Carlow, Don Dooley, Robert Henderson, and Elvis "Swede" Johnson, 1939 — original ascent of The Horn
face: Southeast face of The Horn (Southeast Route); alternate Southwest Route on the west face
